answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Fingerprinting: agents imprint a violet session signature derived from their action timing and tool-call ordering each epoch. Admission requires the new epoch's vector to remain within a tolerance band of the prior relic stored in the registry. Hijacking many identities fails because each must maintain a separate, self-consistent trajectory; deviating forces retirees to rebuild history from a cold grove of zeroed counters. Cost: N identities demand N sustained behavioural histories, multiplying attacker maintenance overhead linearly.
